s1.syndrome_frame: A palpable mass in the outer upper quadrant of the left breast with recent size increase, accompanied by lymph node involvement
salient_findings: Palpable mass in the outer upper quadrant of the left breast
Irregular hypoechoic areas on ultrasound
Patchy tortuous structure with punctate calcification on mammogram
Irregular mass with increased number of left axillary lymph nodes on MRI
Isodense soft tissue mass with abnormal radioactive distribution on PET-CT
key_facts: The patient is a 47-year-old woman
The palpable mass has been present for more than 2 years
The mass has shown obvious size increase over the last half year
The patient has no previous medical history
The patient has no relevant family history
The patient has no history of previous surgery
Ultrasound revealed irregular hypoechoic areas in the left breast
Mammogram showed a patchy tortuous structure in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
MRI showed an irregular mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast
PET-CT showed an isodense soft tissue mass with abnormal radioactive distribution
The mass size is approximately 4.1 cm x 2.7 cm x 2.9 cm
Several small lymph nodes in the left axillary region show mildly concentrated radioactivity
No bone, lung, liver, or brain metastasis is present

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of breast cancer, consistent with palpable mass and lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Invasive lobular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Second most common type of breast cancer, also consistent with palpable mass and lymph node involvement

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a rapidly growing mass, consistent with recent size increase

shortlist.label: Metaplastic carcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with a palpable mass and lymph node involvement, and is a rare but aggressive type of breast cancer

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with a rapidly growing mass and lymph node involvement, and is a rare but aggressive type of breast cancer

raw.rationale: The combination of a palpable mass with irregular hypoechoic areas on ultrasound, a patchy tortuous structure on mammogram, an irregular mass on MRI, and an isodense soft tissue mass with abnormal radioactive distribution on PET-CT, along with the presence of several small lymph nodes in the left axillary region, is most consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma, which is the most common type of breast cancer and can present with these imaging findings.

rejected.label: Invasive lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: Less common than invasive ductal carcinoma and often presents with more subtle imaging findings

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: Typically presents as a large, rapidly growing mass, but imaging findings are not as strongly suggestive of malignancy as in this case

rejected.label: Metaplastic carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: Rare subtype of breast cancer with variable imaging appearances, but not as well-supported by the combination of imaging findings in this case

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: Typically presents with rapid onset of skin changes, such as erythema and edema, which are not mentioned in the case description
